Local Tastes
Mangú
Mashed green plantains topped with sautéed red onions, fried cheese and a fried egg; the Dominican breakfast staple, served at every local comedor from 7:00am onwards.
Local comedores · Bávaro village
Sancocho
A slow-cooked stew of seven meats with root vegetables, yuca and herbs; the Sunday comfort dish of the DR; thick, filling and best eaten at a family-run restaurant in Higüey or Bayahibe.
Family restaurants · Bayahibe or Higüey
Tostones
Twice-fried green plantain discs, salted and served with garlic dipping sauce; sold everywhere from beach vendors to sit-down restaurants and almost always listed as a side.
Captain Cook's and most local restaurants · El Cortecito
Mamajuana
Tree bark and herbs steeped in rum, red wine and honey; the Dominican folk remedy and conversation starter; sold in small recycled bottles at beach markets and souvenir stalls.
Beach markets · El Cortecito and Bávaro
Food Delivery
Rappi
Foreign number: accepted. — SMS verification code delivers to the foreign number without issue; US, Canadian and European numbers confirmed to receive the OTP.
Good selection of local restaurants, convenience stores and pharmacy delivery in the Bávaro zone; grocery and alcohol delivery available; delivery times run 35–60 minutes on the resort strip.
rappi.com.do
PedidosYa
Foreign number: accepted. — OTP arrives by SMS on foreign numbers; country-code selector includes US, Canadian and European numbers.
Broader restaurant selection than Rappi in El Cortecito and Bávaro village, including local comedores and Dominican fast food not found on other platforms; delivery times 40–70 minutes.
pedidosya.com.do

Getting Around
Uber
Foreign number: accepted. — verification SMS arrives reliably on foreign numbers; US, Canadian and European numbers all confirmed to receive the OTP.
Reliable across the Bávaro–Cap Cana corridor; flat rates quoted before booking with no surge on standard routes; GPS routing handles the resort zone well; drivers pick up promptly at hotel entrances.
uber.com
InDriver
Foreign number: accepted. — OTP arrives by SMS; sign up with international country code before arrival to save time.
Consistently cheaper than Uber for longer trips such as Higüey, Altos de Chavón and La Romana; bidding model means you propose a fare and the driver accepts or counters, typically landing 20–30% below Uber's quoted price on the same route.
indriver.com
Worth Knowing

Currency — the Dominican peso — DOP — is the official currency; US dollars are widely accepted at tourist spots but change is returned in pesos at unfavourable hotel rates. One trip to an in-town ATM in Bávaro or Higüey covers the day far more cheaply than withdrawing at resort cashiers.

Tourist card — a tourist card — DOP 1,500 per person — is required for entry; major airlines flying direct into Punta Cana International Airport now include it in the ticket price, but check before departure to avoid paying again at immigration.

Sun timing — the Caribbean sun at 18°N burns quickly even through cloud cover; reef-safe sunscreen is required at Hoyo Azul, the ecological park and the Del Este National Park, and is requested voluntarily at Natural Pool and Saona Island.

All-inclusive rhythm — resort buffet restaurants hit peak crowding in the first fifteen minutes after each meal's official opening; arriving five minutes before the crowd or ten minutes after it disperses avoids the queue entirely.

Catamaran tours — the Saona Island day trips fill from the same limited fleet; book the night before through the hotel concierge or any tour kiosk in El Cortecito, not the morning of — sold-out boats are common in high season.
